arxiv-1904-08173.title: d-orthogonal polynomials, Toda Lattice and Virasoro symmetries
arxiv-1904-08173.creator: Emil Horozov
arxiv-1904-08173.description: Abstract . The subject of this paper is a connection between d-orthogonal polynomials and the Toda lattice hierarchy. In more details we consider some polynomial systems similar to Hermite polynomials, but satisfying d + 2 d+2 -term recurrence relation, d > 1 d>1 . Any such polynomial system defines a solution of the Toda lattice hierarchy.

arxiv-2009-14735.description: Abstract Using the Monte-Carlo method, we study the magnetic properties of the Ashkin-Teller model (ATM) under the effect of the crystal field with spins S = 1 S=1 and σ = 3 / 2 \sigma=3/2 . First, we determine the most stable phases in the phase diagrams at temperature T = 0 T=0 using exact calculations.

arxiv-2107-07310.title: The primordial black hole from running curvaton
arxiv-2107-07310.creator: Lei-Hua Liu 1
arxiv-2107-07310.description: Abstract In light of our previous work Liu:2019xhn , we investigate the possibility of the formation of a primordial black hole in the second inflationary process induced by the oscillation of curvaton. By adopting the instability of the Mathieu equation, one could utilize the δ \delta function to fully describe the power spectrum.

arxiv-2204-13548.title: Tragedy Plus Time : Capturing Unintended Human Activities from Weakly-labeled Videos
arxiv-2204-13548.creator: Arnav Chakravarthy, Zhiyuan Fang, Yezhou Yang
arxiv-2204-13548.description: Abstract In videos that contain actions performed unintentionally, agents do not achieve their desired goals. In such videos, it is challenging for computer vision systems to understand high-level concepts such as goal-directed behavior, an ability present in humans from a very early age.

arxiv-2405-13730.title: Subspace Mixed Finite Elements for Real-Time Heterogeneous Elastodynamics
arxiv-2405-13730.creator: Ty Trusty, Otman Benchekroun, Eitan Grinspun, Danny M. Kaufman, David I.W. Levin
arxiv-2405-13730.description: Abstract . Real-time elastodynamic solvers are well-suited for the rapid simulation of homogeneous elastic materials, with high-rates generally enabled by aggressive early termination of timestep solves. Unfortunately, the introduction of strong domain heterogeneities can make these solvers slow to converge. Stopping the solve short creates visible damping artifacts and rotational errors.

arxiv-2407-05494.title: Prospective Messaging: Learning in Networks with Communication Delays
arxiv-2407-05494.creator: Ryan Fayyazi, Christian Weilbach, Frank WoodDepartment of Computer ScienceUniversity of British ColumbiaVancouver, Canada {rfayyazi,weilbach,fwood}@cs.ubc.ca
arxiv-2407-05494.description: Abstract Inter-neuron communication delays are ubiquitous in physically realized neural networks such as biological neural circuits and neuromorphic hardware. These delays have significant and often disruptive consequences on network dynamics during training and inference. It is therefore essential that communication delays be accounted for, both in computational models of biological neural networks and in large-scale neuromorphic systems.

pmc-10751488.title: Microglial process dynamics depend on astrocyte and synaptic activity
pmc-10751488.creator: Ako Ikegami, Daisuke Kato, Hiroaki Wake
pmc-10751488.description: Microglial processes survey the brain parenchyma, but it is unknown whether this process is influenced by the cell activity of nearby microglia under physiological conditions. Herein, we showed that microglial process dynamics differ when facilitated by astrocytic activity and pre-synaptic activity. The results revealed distinct microglial process dynamics associated with the activity of other brain cells.

pmc-11303033.title: Short-term dietary changes are reflected in the cerebral content of adult ring-billed gulls
pmc-11303033.creator: Jessika Lamarre, David R. Wilson
pmc-11303033.description: Omega-3 long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acids (n3-LCPUFAs) are produced primarily in aquatic ecosystems and are considered essential nutrients for predators given their structural role in vertebrates’ cerebral tissues. Alarmingly, with urbanization, many aquatic animals now rely on anthropogenic foods lacking n3-LCPUFAs.

pmc-11394778.title: A Systematic Review of Online Medical Consultation Research
pmc-11394778.creator: Tian Shen, Yu Li, Xi Chen, Mustafa Z Younis
pmc-11394778.description: Online medical consultation is a form of medical service that facilitates interactions between patients and doctors online, offering significant utility and value. This review aims to retrieve, screen, and analyze articles related to online medical consultations, formulating a theoretical framework and proposing future research directions.

pmc-11521853.title: Identification of middle cerebral artery stenosis in transcranial Doppler using a modified VGG-16
pmc-11521853.creator: Dong Xu, Hao Li, Fanghui Su, Sizheng Qiu, Huixia Tong, Meifeng Huang, Jianzhong Yao
pmc-11521853.description: ObjectivesThe diagnosis of intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis (ICAS) is of great significance for the prevention of stroke. Deep learning (DL)-based artificial intelligence techniques may aid in the diagnosis. The study aimed to identify ICAS in the middle cerebral artery (MCA) based on a modified DL model.MethodsThis retrospective study included two datasets.

pmc-11677464.title: The Use of Technology in the Prevention of Infections Associated with Urinary Catheterization
pmc-11677464.creator: Bruna Raquel Fonseca, Maura Filipa Silva, Rogério Ferrinho Ferreira, Sofia Cabecinhas de Sá, Teresa Dionísio Mestre, Marta Sofia Catarino, Richard Gray, Niall S Higgins
pmc-11677464.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). (1) Background: Urinary tract infections (UTIs) are caused by the proliferation of pathogenic microorganisms, and they are the second most common hospital-acquired infections, with catheter-associated UTIs (CAUTIs) accounting for about 40% of these nosocomial infections.

pmc-11774732.title: Prevalence and risk factors for long COVID among cancer patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-11774732.creator: Hongkun Xu, Tingting Lu, Yajie Liu, Jingqi Yang, Simeng Ren, Baojin Han, Honghao Lai, Long Ge, Jie Liu
pmc-11774732.description: ObjectiveThe prevalence of long COVID among cancer patients remains unknown. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of long COVID and explore potential risk factors among cancer patients.MethodsA systematic search was performed on PubMed, Web of Science, and Embase from database inception until 21 March 2024, to identify studies that reported long COVID in cancer patients.

pmc-12702600.title: Dysfunctions of Reward Motivation Adaptation in Patients With Schizophrenia
pmc-12702600.creator: Yiming Pan, Hui Wang, Qi Zhou, Bingjie Huang, Chengcheng Pu, Simon S Y Lui, Jia Huang, Raymond C K Chan
pmc-12702600.description: Diminished reward motivation in the wanting or liking dimension constitutes one of the core dysfunctions in patients with schizophrenia (SCZ). However, it remains unclear whether patients with SCZ would dynamically adapt their wanting or liking towards reward in response to a favourable effort‐reward ratio and whether such adaptation correlates with their clinical symptoms or functional outcome.

pmc-12734447.title: Effects of the Pharmacological Modulation of NRF2 in Cancer Progression
pmc-12734447.creator: Santiago Gelerstein-Claro, Gabriel Méndez-Valdés, Ramón Rodrigo, Robert Ancuceanu
pmc-12734447.description: Nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2) orchestrates redox balance, metabolism, and cellular stress responses, acting as both a tumor suppressor and promoter depending on the disease stage. In advanced cancers, persistent NRF2 activation—through KEAP1/NFE2L2 mutations or oxidative adaptation—drives epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, metabolic reprogramming, and immune evasion, promoting tumor invasion (T) and metastasis (M).

pmc-13325570.title: 25-year follow-up of 102 unrevised cementless total hip arthroplasties with a second-generation metal-on-metal bearing in a young patient cohort
pmc-13325570.creator: Moritz von Falkenhayn, Andre Lunz, Max Kempe, Timo A Nees, Kevin-Arno Koch, Moritz M Innmann, Tilman Walker, Tobias Reiner
pmc-13325570.description: BackgroundSecond-generation metal-on-metal (MoM) bearings were reintroduced in total hip arthroplasty (THA) for their low wear rates, but despite initially promising results, concerns have emerged about adverse reactions to metal debris and poor long-term implant survival, with limited and conflicting evidence regarding the outcomes of small-diameter MoM implants.

pmc-13349121.title: A qualitative analysis of Chinese novice general dentists’ perspectives on using ergonomic loupes in clinical practice
pmc-13349121.creator: Kexian Xie, Yuangao Li, Xiao Wang, Ning Ma
pmc-13349121.description: BackgroundErgonomic loupes are the next-generation loupes with built-in refractive prisms that enable the user to sit up straight, look straight ahead, and reduce neck tilt while viewing the operating field from down below. They differ greatly from traditional loupes in optic design and viewer perspective. They appeared on the market in 2022 and are quickly gaining popularity in China.

pmc-13569972.title: Single‐Step Synthesis of Dithieno[3,2‐b:2′,3′‐e]Pyridines and Their Acid‐Dependent Optical and Photosensitising Properties
pmc-13569972.creator: Dominic Taylor, Matthew Wallace, Leonardo Amicosante, Gary S. Nichol, Scott J. Dalgarno, Filipe Vilela, Iain A. Wright, Neil B. McKeown
pmc-13569972.description: Dithieno[3,2‐b:2‘,3’‐e]pyridine (DTP) is a heterocycle consisting of a central pyridine ring fused with two thiophene rings and can be regarded as a thiophene‐based analogue of the classic N‐heterocycle acridine. Unlike acridine‐based dyes, the fundamental chemistry of DTP has received relatively little attention.

pmc-13577254.title: Circular RNA functions in HIV-1 infection
pmc-13577254.creator: Gabriela Berger, Y. Grace Chen
pmc-13577254.description: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) are covalently closed RNA molecules with increasingly recognized roles in post-transcriptional gene regulation, immune signalling, and host–pathogen interactions. Although circRNAs have been characterized across diverse biological contexts, their roles in viral infection, particularly HIV-1, remain an underexplored area of RNA biology. Here, we review current knowledge of circRNA function in HIV-1 infection, organized into three major themes.

pmc-13604709.title: The Role of Circulating Extracellular DNA in Patients with Bladder Cancer: Clinical Associations and Exploratory Links with Heart Rate Variability
pmc-13604709.creator: Patrik Palacka, Hana Kováčová Ilijew, Iveta Mikolášková, Magda Suchánková, Mária Paulovičová, Beáta Rondziková, Boris Kollárik, Peter Celec, Ľuba Hunáková
pmc-13604709.description: Simple SummaryThis study investigated plasma extracellular DNA—including nuclear (ncDNA) and mitochondrial (mtDNA) fractions—and DNase activity in 63 bladder cancer (BC) patients and 21 healthy controls. The findings reveal that circulating extracellular DNA and ncDNA are independently associated with BC, with ncDNA showing particularly strong associations with advanced tumor stages (muscle-invasive BC).
